source: MAFF General Directorate of Agriculture / CAVAC rice variety catalog for production and export (elibrary source; no clear URL visible on the scanned pages provided)
text: Phka Rumdoul (ផ្កាដូល) appears in this MAFF/CAVAC catalog of Cambodia's principal rice varieties as one of the medium-duration, photoperiod-sensitive (rainy-season) varieties recommended for production, alongside varieties such as Riang Chey. Photoperiod-sensitive varieties like this one flower in response to shortening day length rather than a fixed number of days after sowing, so they are typically grown once per year in the wet season with harvest timed to that natural flowering response (commonly around November in Cambodia). The catalog highlights Phka Rumdoul's grain quality as suited to both domestic consumption and export - this variety is widely known outside this source as Cambodia's flagship premium fragrant rice, the basis of much of the country's rice export reputation, though that broader context comes from general knowledge rather than this particular document.
